A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Point-MoE research despite changed titles and framing. All 37 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation experiments, architectural ablations, domain-classifier results, and expert-routing analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original segmentation and routing results and adds experiments involving OA-CNN, mixed-dataset batching, and computational efficiency.

M1.justification: V2 removes the domain-conditioned gating and 20% generic-domain randomization variants, while adding a top-2 sparse-convolution MoE adaptation to OA-CNN BasicBlocks (Appendix B.2). The core PTv3/CLIP framework remains. Output-projection placement is clarified, but v1's conflicting prose and diagram do not establish that this clarification itself represents an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions cover ScanNet, Structured3D, S3DIS, Matterport3D, nuScenes, SemanticKITTI, and Waymo for 3D semantic segmentation. Indoor/outdoor, real/synthetic, and held-out dataset coverage remains unchanged; the revisions concern architectures and experimental procedures within this coverage.

E2.justification: OA-CNNs becomes an evaluated comparator in v2 Table 1a, with further OA-CNN versus OA-CNN-MoE comparisons in Table 11. Table 4 also evaluates a mixed-batch-compatible PPT implementation. PTv3 and PPT combined with One-for-All-style dataset prediction remain the primary baselines.

E3.justification: Reported training budgets increase from 120k to 140k indoor iterations and 160k to 180k indoor-outdoor iterations (v1 Table 8; v2 Table 10). V2 removes oracle-ID and generic-ID evaluation controls, adds mixed-batching controls, and introduces average-score and FLOP/peak-memory measurements. Precise versus non-precise evaluation was already documented in v1.

E4.justification: Table 3d replaces decoder-only versus whole-network MoE placement with FFN versus attention-output projection placement. V2 adds mixed-batching controls for PPT and Point-MoE and a convolutional-backbone applicability test. V1's single-dataset Point-MoE diagnostic, oracle-label controls, and training/validation curves disappear. The t-SNE, JSD, and extensive appendix routing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. V2's added averages summarize benchmark scores rather than run-to-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Numerous main and appendix results change. Indoor Point-MoE-L Structured3D validation changes from 73.0 to 69.5, and Matterport3D test from 47.8 to 46.7; indoor-outdoor SemanticKITTI changes from 63.2 to 66.4. Changed reported budgets prevent treating these as same-setting performance changes. OA-CNN and efficiency results are added, while domain-conditioned and single-dataset Point-MoE result blocks are removed.

T1.justification: V1's explicit domain-conditioned gating definition is removed, while v2 Section 3.1 formalizes the distinction between shared-parameter and dataset-specific-parameter objectives. The underlying supervised objective, top-k mixture, and appendix weighted-JSD definition remain equivalent. No theorem or proof is introduced; the added standard attention equations primarily clarify the architecture.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from cross-domain generalization explored through both domain-aware and domain-agnostic variants to unified heterogeneous multi-dataset training without dataset IDs for Point-MoE during training or inference. V2 foregrounds this protocol, systematic design exploration, and performance across seven datasets. Generalization to unseen datasets remains a central claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving attention-output fusion, shared normalization statistics, and competition among experts during mixed batching. It removes the discussion of inconclusive single-dataset benefits and domain-randomization effects. Appendix A.1 drops routing-overhead and unregularized-specialization caveats while adding annotation-cost limitations. The earlier acknowledged Structured3D specialist gap is replaced by an overbroad specialist-matching interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies encoder/decoder depths, small/large expert dimensions, and S3DIS Area5, and clarifies dense QKV versus MoE output projection. It also documents the OA-CNN adaptation. Conversely, v1's explicit 0.02 m indoor and 0.05 m outdoor voxel sizes disappear. Most optimizer, scheduler, and batch-size details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated domain-generalization discussion distinguishing heterogeneous joint training from fixed-target transfer. Related work expands to Sonata, UniDet3D, MoE3D, and several LiDAR generalization methods, among others. The novelty positioning changes from MoE for cross-domain generalization to MoE for multi-dataset point-cloud training.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method exposition, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Section 3 gains separate task-formulation and architecture subsections, results are organized around seen versus zero-shot evaluation, and the t-SNE discussion moves from the appendix into the main text. These changes substantially reorganize the paper.

P2.justification: Main Tables 1–2 are rebuilt into seen/zero-shot panels with average columns. V2 adds batching and efficiency tables, redraws Figure 1, and expands Figure 3 using additional routing views. The training-curve figure disappears, while appendix t-SNE becomes main Figure 2. Most later appendix visualizations remain unchanged apart from layout and numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves conflicting MoE-placement descriptions and adds useful batching controls, a convolutional-backbone test, and direct compute/memory measurements, providing a limited net gain in clarity and evidential support. Benefits are tempered by removed diagnostic results and voxel settings, and an overstated specialist comparison: v2 Table 1a still reports 69.5 versus 81.5 on Structured3D validation.
